The Boardwalk hotel is worth $2000, which would bankrupt the opponent if their liquidation is roughly $1683. The Park Place hotel is only $1500, so it would not finish them off. I will keep Illinois at two houses to drain cash while maintaining even building across the reds.

I realized my reds are uneven: one house on Indiana and two on Illinois. I should build on Kentucky and Indiana to match. I am now calculating the opponent's liquidation value.

I am calculating the opponent's liquidation value by selling their hotels for half their purchase price. I am also recalling standard house prices by color to determine how much cash they would have if forced to sell all buildings.

I am now calculating the exact cash value of each opponent's hotel if forced to sell. A Mediterranean hotel sells for $25, which reverts it to four houses worth $100 total. The bank still has 28 houses and 8 hotels available.

Baltic hotel also sells for $125, so the opponent's buildings total $250. I am now listing mortgage values for their remaining unmortgaged properties to complete the liquidation estimate.

The opponent's liquidation totals $1683. Boardwalk hotel rent is $2000, so they cannot pay and will go bankrupt. Park Place hotel rent is only $1500, which they can afford with leftover cash. The kill shot must be Boardwalk.

The opponent may stay in jail to avoid Boardwalk. I cannot force them onto that space. I will not trade them cash or properties that would help them survive the $2000 hotel rent.

Building on Kentucky and Indiana would cost $300, leaving me with $220 cash. I am now calculating the rent values for red properties once they are fully upgraded.

I confirmed the official rent schedule for red properties. Indiana and Kentucky each cost $90 per house. Illinois costs $100 per house. Two houses on Illinois equals $300 in rent.

Building more reds would not finish the opponent off. An Illinois hotel still leaves them with roughly $570 in liquidation, which is survivable. I also need to keep cash on hand to pay their brown hotels if I land there. A single house costs $150 and would leave me with only $370, which is too little to cover a Baltic hotel hit of $450 without selling buildings first.

Selling the Boardwalk hotel would drop its rent from $2000 to $1700. That is still $17 short of the opponent's liquidation of $1683, so it would barely finish them off. If I must sell that hotel to pay rent, I lose the kill shot. Landing on Baltic with only $520 leaves me with just $70 cash.

I will keep the Boardwalk hotel intact. If I must sell it to pay rent, the rent drops to $1700 and I may need to sell more houses to survive. Rent from utilities and railroads is manageable. The only dangerous squares are the brown hotels.

I need to keep $450 cash to survive a Baltic hotel hit without selling the Boardwalk hotel. I will not spend any money this turn. Unmortgaging properties would cost extra interest and is not worth it. I am checking which color sets are complete.

I do not own complete color sets among my mortgaged properties. Unmortgaging would only yield modest rent, so it is not worth the cost.

I considered trading my mortgaged Pennsylvania Avenue to the opponent. That would complete their green color set and give them a major income boost. I rejected this because it would help them survive the Boardwalk hotel rent.

I considered trading my mortgaged Ventnor Avenue, but the opponent still needs Atlantic to complete a yellow monopoly. That would not finish me off immediately, though it is still undesirable.

I am now looking for a trade that gives me cash without handing the opponent a dangerous color set. Their Get Out of Jail Free card is not useful to me, but taking it would force them to roll or pay $50 to leave jail eventually.

Taking the opponent's Get Out of Jail Free card would force them onto the board where they can land on Boardwalk. I rejected a cash-for-GOOJF offer because it would reduce my own cash buffer while giving them money to survive the hotel rent. I also realized that offering any mortgaged property in exchange would increase their liquidation value, since they could mortgage it.

I realized that giving the opponent a mortgaged property would not increase their liquidation value. They cannot mortgage it again for cash, so that trade would not help them survive the Boardwalk hotel rent.

Mortgaged Pennsylvania Avenue would complete the opponent's green color set. They would unmortgage it for $176 and build houses, turning Pacific, North Carolina, and Pennsylvania Avenue into hotels that cost $1275 to $1400 each. That is far too dangerous to trade.

I confirmed that giving away mortgaged properties would not complete any color sets for the opponent. They already own Oriental, so neither Vermont nor Connecticut would finish a light blue set. Ventnor is also not worth trading since it cannot complete their yellow set.

I also considered trading both Vermont and Connecticut to the opponent. That would complete a light blue monopoly, though it would not instantly bankrupt me. I still refuse to give them any color set that could become dangerous.

I also checked whether giving away States Avenue would complete a pink monopoly for them. They already own Virginia and St Charles, so that trade would indeed finish their pink set.

I confirmed that giving away States Avenue would complete the opponent's pink color set. Orange properties and railroads are also not worth trading, since they do not finish a set and would only slightly increase their rent. I am now considering whether to ask the opponent for cash or their Get Out of Jail Free card in exchange for nothing.

I rejected the idea of proposing a deceptive trade. The opponent is smart and would reject bad offers, so I will not waste a turn action on a proposal that could backfire.

I am now calculating how much cash I need to take from the opponent. Their liquidation is $1683, which is $317 short of the $2000 Boardwalk hotel rent. If they pass GO and collect $200, their liquidation rises to $1883, leaving only a $117 gap. Any extra cash would shrink that margin further.

I realized that if the opponent lands on Baltic before hitting Boardwalk, they gain $450 and their liquidation becomes $2133. That is enough to survive the $2000 hotel rent with $133 left over. The order of landings matters. I cannot control dice to avoid landing on Baltic. I am now looking for a way to force them to spend cash so that even a Baltic rent would not save them.

I calculated that the opponent must be liquidated below $1350 to survive a Baltic rent plus passing GO. Currently their liquidation is $1683, so I need to extract roughly $333 or destroy their assets. I cannot destroy their properties directly; only rent payments can reduce them. If they land on my properties before I land on Baltic, they pay rent and are nearly bankrupt.

Building three houses on Illinois Avenue would raise rent to $750, but it costs $150 in construction and leaves only $370 cash. That is still too little to cover a Baltic hotel hit of $450 without selling more buildings. This exposes the core cash management problem.

I will not build houses this turn. The minimum construction cost is $150, leaving only $370 cash after building. That is still $80 short of the $450 Baltic hotel rent. Selling one Illinois house for $75 would leave me $5 short. I cannot sell more houses from Illinois without violating the rule that requires keeping at least as many houses on Illinois as on Kentucky or Indiana.

I can sell one house from each of the three red properties, since they are all at one house. That would raise cash by $225, but it would also reduce rent on those properties. It still does not force the opponent to sell their Boardwalk hotel.

Building one house is not worth the cost, since the rent increase would not kill them and I would still need to sell more buildings to cover a Baltic hotel hit. I will not unmortgage properties either, because that costs money and does not complete a color set. I am now considering whether to propose a deceptive trade that offers the opponent something they want in exchange for cash, though I expect them to reject it.

I am now considering a trade that would buy the opponent's brown hotels. That would eliminate the $450 and $250 rent threat from Mediterranean and Baltic, but paying cash for those properties would give them money to survive the Boardwalk hotel.

I calculated that buying both brown hotels would cost roughly $200, netting the opponent a $110 loss while leaving them still bankrupt to Boardwalk. They would never accept such an offer. I am now looking for a trade that gives them a viable path to survive or kill me.

I considered trading mortgaged Pennsylvania Avenue to the opponent for cash. That would give them a green monopoly and extra cash, but it would also let them build hotels costing over $1400 each. I rejected this trade because it is too dangerous.

I will end my turn. I will not trade away any color set that could become dangerous, including green, pink, or light blue properties. I will keep my public message brief and avoid revealing strategy.

I confirmed the opponent's liquidation is $1683. Boardwalk hotel at $2000 leaves a $317 gap, while four houses on Baltic at $1700 leaves only a $17 gap. I have a $70 cushion against the $450 Baltic hotel rent. The opponent is in jail with a Get Out of Jail Free card and may stay there to avoid the board. I cannot force them out without giving them more resources. I am now considering whether to attempt one last probe trade for their card.

I considered offering a mortgaged railroad for the opponent's Get Out of Jail Free card. That trade would not add liquidation, and the rent from one mortgaged railroad is only $50 until unmortgaged. The opponent would reject it because jail safety is worth more than the mortgage cost.
